chapter: Minstrel show life and Ida Cox
title: Minstrel versus carnival shows
summary: He explains minstrel one-nighters versus carnival jig shows, tents, trucks and railroad cars, and the concert admission.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah. This wasn't a carnival show then that Bessie was with. It was just...

Oh, a minstrel show. See, it's different between... A minstrel. A minstrel, you could call it one-nighters. You see, a minstrel played one-nighters. On a carnival show you had a minstrel show too, but they used to call it a jig show.
Why they called it a jig show is on the kind of jigging they call it, and they used to call it a jig show, you see. Yeah.

And well, I mean they had different shows like the ten and one athletic show and so forth, and the Hawaiian show, and the jig show. Yeah. But now, on a minstrel show, most of the time they used a car, you see. You have a special railroad car, you see. And maybe two or three trucks that, you know, with this particular show...
Yeah, they'd carry a lot of things like rides and Ferris wheels and things like that, I guess. Well, that's on the carnival, you see.
Yeah, on the carnival. Well now, a minstrel show only carried a show, that's all. Just a big top.
You always have a tent with you then. That's right.

Now this old man, old man Palmer, it was his show, see. Well he had a car, and he sold a car, see. And he started using trucks. He figured, I mean, it'd be cheaper using trucks and bus to all the people, instead of using it, because railroad cars cost a lot of money. I mean, even to pull a car, man, out and transport from one track to another, and all that kind of stuff, I mean, it cost a lot of money. It's like circus. Yeah.

This reel is just about over. I was going to ask about the show again. In this show that Bessie Smith is with, everybody traveled in the bus then except Bessie, or were there some more cars too? Well, the stage manager, he had a car.
He and his wife. That's right. He had a car. And that was a tent show then, that first had the minstrel show, then after that would be the concert.

See, everybody would leave out. They'd have to leave the tent, then they'd pay to get back in again. They'd pay to come back in. Which used to be sometime 25 or made it 35 cents, according to what towns you were in, you know
